titulo: From chat to queue: why save tasks
lead: In chat, the agent does one thing at a time and only while the window is open. A durable queue stores each request, runs one at a time, resumes after a crash, and separates what worked from what failed.
objetivo: explain the four guarantees of a durable queue and why they let you step away.
hero_alt: A row of paper cards arranged in sequence on a dark table, with one card highlighted.

aprende.t: The limit of chat: you have to keep watching
The four guarantees of a durable queue
Task states, from request to result

secoes.sub: The same request, in two different places.

itens.t: Close the window, lose the work

nos.detalhe: In chat, you type, wait, copy, and paste. If you close the window or the computer shuts down, the work in progress disappears. Ten tasks = ten waits with you in front.
The request is saved before it runs. In inemaccbot, the queue is a SQLite database on disk; in the homemade queue, it’s one file per task in a folder. Shut down? The task is still there.

nos.sub: Picks up one at a time
nos.detalhe: A worker picks up a task, hands it to the agent, and waits. If the process crashes midway, on the next startup it recovers what was in flight before accepting new work.
Each task ends in a clear state: it worked (with the file or text) or it failed (with the reason). That’s what you check in the morning.

secoes.volta: Running it again only picks up what’s left
secoes.legenda: In inemaccbot, the request comes through Telegram; in the homemade queue from lesson 3, it’s an .md file in a folder. The idea is the same.

rolagem_fim.titulo: Why this lets you step away
rolagem_fim.texto: Save before running, one at a time, resume after a crash, and separate done from failed: with these four guarantees, turning off the screen doesn’t cost you work.

secoes.sub: What you should expect from any queue, homemade or otherwise.

texto: The request becomes a record on disk as soon as it arrives. It doesn’t depend on an open window or the program’s memory.
In inemaccbot, each request becomes a job in a database table. It has a number (j13), a queue, a status, and a number of attempts remaining.

exemplo.rot: What this looks like day to day
exemplo.texto: You send the request from your phone, the computer restarts, and the request is still in the list.

texto: Each worker picks up a task, finishes it, and only then picks up the next one. This keeps two jobs from competing for the same machine.
In inemaccbot, there are five queues with different limits: the render queue runs one at a time on purpose because it uses the graphics card; the network queue accepts ten.
If the process crashes midway, the task isn’t lost or left half done forever. On the next startup, anything in progress goes back into the queue.

inemaccbot does this before accepting new work and writes to the log: boot: recuperação de leases — requeued=N failed=M. Requeued means it went back into the queue; failed means it had already used up all its attempts.
A task that errors doesn’t disappear or block the queue: it goes to the failures side, with the reason recorded, and the queue moves on.
inemaccbot prompts require the agent to finish with RESULT: <path> or ERRO: <short reason>. This contract lets you know how each task ended without opening anything.

secoes.sub: The names change from one queue to another; the idea is the same.

blocos.conteudo:
fila/
  entrada/   # requests waiting their turn
  rodando/   # the task the agent is working on now
  feito/     # request + response
  falhou/    # request + ERRO and the reason

queued    # in the queue, waiting its turn
running   # a worker picked it up and is running it
done      # finished with a result
failed    # ran out of attempts, with the reason
canceled  # you canceled it (/cancelar)

abas.html:
• Homemade queue: when you run it again, anything in rodando/ goes back to entrada/.
  • inemaccbot: the worker renews a task “lease” while it works. If the lease expires because the process crashed, the task goes back to queued as long as attempts remain.

In the homemade queue: an empty response or an error code from the agent. In inemaccbot: the agent didn't finish with RESULT:, the deadline (timeout) expired, or the attempts (max_tentativas, 2 to 4 in the catalog skills) ran out.

secoes.sub: inemaccbot's durable queue and approval gate, in a minute and a half.
The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What's the essential difference between asking in chat and sending something to a durable queue?
opcoes: The queue uses a better AI model.
The queue request is saved to disk before it runs, so it doesn't depend on you or on the window staying open.
You can't ask for long tasks in chat.
perguntas.explica: The model can be the same. What changes is where the request goes: it becomes a durable record, so it survives crashes and can run while you're away.

perguntas.p: The bot log showed requeued=2 failed=1 on startup. What happened?
opcoes: The previous process crashed while work was in progress: two tasks went back to the queue, and one had already run out of attempts.
Two tasks succeeded and one failed.
The database was deleted and recreated.
perguntas.explica: This line appears on startup and shows there was work in progress when the process crashed. Requeued means it went back to the queue; failed means there were no attempts left.

perguntas.p: A task failed at 3 a.m. What does a good queue do?
opcoes: Stops everything until you wake up.
Deletes the task so it doesn't get in the way.
Records the failure and the reason, then moves on to the next task.
Keeps retrying forever until it works.
perguntas.explica: The failure is recorded separately with a reason, and the queue keeps moving. Retrying forever would burn through the night (and money), so there's a maximum number of attempts.
